title: Second special sitting of 2024
summary: The Majlis held its second special sitting outside the regular session and debated, at first reading stage, a government bill to amend the Companies Act (Law No. 7/2023), shortening notice periods for company meetings and easing how directors are appointed. Eleven members spoke: most supported the bill, while some opposition members questioned why a special sitting was needed and raised the state of the economy. The sitting paused, then the Majlis voted 77-0 to accept the bill and sent it to the Economic Committee.

items.title: Opening prayer and start of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 59 present at the start, 3 on leave, none on official travel

items.title: Announcement of the day's agenda (agenda no. 20/2024/Special 2)
First-stage debate: bill to amend the Companies Act (Law No. 7/2023), submitted by Feydhoo North member Ismail Nizar for the government
items.outcome: debated by 11 members; debate closed by the chair

items.title: Vote on accepting the Companies Act amendment bill
items.outcome: passed 77-0; referred to the Economic Committee

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Said the amendment makes company meeting procedures and director appointments clearer and notice periods more workable, and strengthens corporate governance and shareholder protection.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the amendment as important for running state companies well and strengthening their governance.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Questioned why a sudden amendment and special sitting were needed, and said companies' real problems are cash flow and unpaid government dues.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the amendment and defended the special sitting, arguing the government wants companies run so they benefit the public.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Said shorter meeting notice would help state companies such as BML and STO act quickly, citing the pending Fenaka takeover by STO.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported shorter notice periods, saying a 21-day wait is unnecessary today, and blamed past governments for company problems.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the amendment, saying companies, public or private, need a strong administrative structure to serve the public quickly.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Backed the amendments as timely and criticised the opposition's remarks and the previous government's handling of state companies.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Noted the changes to articles 100 and 113 and asked what benefit the bill has delivered, while criticising the government over living costs.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked what the purpose of the special sitting is, arguing the notice-period changes are small and political appointments could result.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Said strong structures help companies serve the nation, and criticised opposition members' record while in government.

decisions: The Majlis accepted the Companies Act (Law No. 7/2023) amendment bill at first reading stage.
The bill was referred to the Economic Committee for study under rule 106(r) of the Majlis rules.
The next sitting was set for 9:00 on Tuesday 17 September 2024.

votes.what: Accepting the Companies Act (Law No. 7/2023) amendment bill (78 members present, 39 needed to pass)
